title: Configure Renovate
body:
Welcome to [Renovate](https://redirect.github.com/renovatebot/renovate)! This is an onboarding PR to help you understand and configure settings before regular Pull Requests begin.

🚦 To activate Renovate, merge this Pull Request. To disable Renovate, simply close this Pull Request unmerged.

📚 See our [Reading List](https://docs.renovatebot.com/reading-list/) for relevant documentation you may be interested in reading.

🔡 Do you want to change how Renovate upgrades your dependencies? Add your custom config to `renovate.json` in this branch. Renovate will update the Pull Request description the next time it runs.



---
### Detected Package Files

 * `go.mod` (gomod)

### Configuration Summary

Based on the default config's presets, Renovate will:

  - Start dependency updates only once this onboarding PR is merged
  - Hopefully safe environment variables to allow users to configure.
  - Show all Merge Confidence badges for pull requests.
  - Enable Renovate Dependency Dashboard creation.
  - Use semantic commit type `fix` for dependencies and `chore` for all others if semantic commits are in use.
  - Ignore `node_modules`, `bower_components`, `vendor` and various test/tests (except for nuget) directories.
  - Group known monorepo packages together.
  - Use curated list of recommended non-monorepo package groupings.
  - Show only the Age and Confidence Merge Confidence badges for pull requests.
  - Apply crowd-sourced package replacement rules.
  - Apply crowd-sourced workarounds for known problems with packages.
  - Ensure that every dependency pinned by digest and sourced from Forgejo contains a link to the commit-to-commit diff
  - Ensure that every dependency pinned by digest and sourced from Gitea contains a link to the commit-to-commit diff
  - Ensure that every dependency pinned by digest and sourced from GitHub.com and Github enterprise contains a link to the commit-to-commit diff
  - Ensure that every dependency pinned by digest and sourced from GitLab.com contains a link to the commit-to-commit diff
  - Correctly link to the source code for golang.org/x packages
  - Link to pkg.go.dev/... for golang.org/x packages' title
  - Provide a link to octochangelog's improved breakdown for Renovate's changelogs

---

### What to Expect

It looks like your repository dependencies are already up-to-date and no Pull Requests will be necessary right away.

If you need any further assistance then you can also [request help here](https://redirect.github.com/renovatebot/renovate/discussions).

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/setup-uv (astral-sh/setup-uv)</summary>

### [`v8.2.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v8.2.0): 🌈 New inputs `quiet` and `download-from-astral-mirror`

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v8.1.0...v8.2.0)

##### Changes

This release brings two new inputs and a few bug fixes.

##### New inputs

Lets talk about the new inputs first.

##### quiet

Pretty simple. It turns of all `info` loggings. Useful if you use this in a composite action and are not interested in all the details.
In the upcoming releases we will add log groups to fully implement support for "less noise"

> \[!NOTE]\
> Warnings and errors are always logged.

##### download-from-astral-mirror

In some cases you may want to directly use the fallback of checking for available versions and downloading releases from GitHub instead of using the astral.sh mirror. Setting `download-from-astral-mirror: false` allows you to do that.

##### Bugfixes

When using the astral.sh mirror to query available versions and download releases (done by default) we now stop sending the GitHub token in the header. The mirror never looked at it but we shouldn't be handing out that data even if it is just a short lived token.
All other bugfixes try to limit the impact of failed GitHub queries due to retries and other faults.

We couldn't pinpoint all rootcauses yet but added more logging for error cases to track them down.

#### Details
A flaw was found in ansible-core. The ansible-galaxy role install command processes dependency specifications from a role's meta/requirements.yml file. Due to improper neutralization of argument delimiters, a malicious role author can inject arbitrary git configuration flags through the src field. This allows arbitrary code execution on the machine of a user who installs the role via ansible-galaxy role install.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/setup-uv (astral-sh/setup-uv)</summary>

### [`v10.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v10.0.0): 🌈 Disable automatic caching for sensitive events and new QOL features

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v9.0.0...v10.0.0)

##### Changes

Another breaking release, directly after v9.0.0 but we think the added security justifies that.

##### Extra security by default

If you use the default `enable-cache: auto` this will now **DISABLE THE CACHE** to protect against cache poisoning for the following events:

- `pull_request_target`
- `workflow_run`
- `release`

You can read the full reasoning in [#​984](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/984)

##### `version: latest-known`

```yaml
- name: Install the latest version of uv known to setup-uv
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.0
  with:
    version: "latest-known"
```

This will now install the latest version with a checksum that is known by this action. The [known `uv` checksums](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/blob/4f6036f71cec78afb113b323f220c9185d983c12/src/download/checksum/known-checksums.ts) are automatically updated but will take a release of this action to take effect. You won't be always using the latest & greatest but you will have an extra level of security.

##### Read python version from `.tool-versions`

```yaml
- name: Install uv based on the version defined in .tool-versions and also set python
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.0
  with:
    version-file: "pyproject.toml"
```

Will now also set the python version if it is defined in `.tool-versions`. You can read the details [in the docs](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/blob/main/docs/advanced-version-configuration.md#install-a-version-defined-in-a-requirements-or-config-file)

#### 29.9.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.9.0 milestone](https://redirect.github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.9.0)
- [moby/moby, 29.9.0 milestone](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.9.0)

##### Security

The Go runtime update fixes the following security vulnerabilities in Docker Engine:

- **CVE-2026-97032**: An HTTP/2 client could crash the daemon by changing the HPACK header table size while sending requests. [golang/go#81867](https://go.dev/issue/81867)
- **CVE-2026-78659**: An HTTP/2 client could exhaust daemon memory by declaring a large number of fields in a `Trailer` header, bypassing the header size limits. [golang/go#81857](https://go.dev/issue/81857)
- **CVE-2026-78663**: An HTTP/2 client could bypass the connection-level flow control limit by resetting streams, making the daemon buffer more request data than the limit allows. [golang/go#81743](https://go.dev/issue/81743)
- **CVE-2026-78669**: An HTTP/2 client could cause excessive daemon CPU use by opening many streams and repeatedly changing the initial window size. [golang/go#81742](https://go.dev/issue/81742)
- **CVE-2026-56857**: On Windows, the daemon could create a directory outside its data root if someone with write access to the data root had placed a junction there. [golang/go#81739](https://go.dev/issue/81739)

The `golang.org/x/net` update to v0.60.0 applies the same HTTP/2 fixes to the deprecated `/grpc` endpoint and to the gRPC server that BuildKit runs for frontend containers, such as images referenced by a `# syntax=` directive.

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- containerd image store: Add the `lazy-pull` daemon feature to control whether `docker pull` skips downloading layer content that the snapshotter already provides. Lazy pulls are enabled by default for known remote snapshotters (`nydus`, `overlaybd`, `soci`, `stargz`). [moby/moby#53877](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53877)
- containerd image store: Fix pulls skipping required layer blobs when unpacked layers already exist, leaving images runnable but incomplete for export or push. [moby/moby#53615](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53615)
- Fix `docker container create --name` reporting a misleading validation error mentioning invalid characters instead of invalid name length. [moby/moby#53484](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53484)
- Fix a connection leak to the RootlessKit API socket on every `GET /version` request in rootless mode. [moby/moby#53836](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53836)
- Improve Windows service registration and unregistration cleanup, including making service unregistration (`--unregister-service`) idempotent. [moby/moby#53845](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53845)

##### Packaging updates

- Update BuildKit to [v0.34.0](https://redirect.github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.34.0). [moby/moby#53882](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53882)
- Update Go runtime to [1.26.9](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#go1.26.9). [docker/cli#7363](https://redirect.github.com/docker/cli/pull/7363)
- Update containerd (static binaries) to [v2.4.1](https://redirect.github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.4.1). [moby/moby#53773](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53773)

##### Networking

- Allow IPv6 Neighbour Discovery between containers on a bridge network with inter-container communication disabled, matching the existing IPv4 behaviour. [moby/moby#53723](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53723)
- Fix `docker ps` and `GET /containers/json` omitting published ports for networks using routed gateway mode. [moby/moby#53693](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53693)
- Fix a bug where a restarted daemon could be dropped from a peer's service discovery and load balancing until it rejoined the gossip cluster. [moby/moby#53688](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53688)
- Fix a published port being unreachable from another container on the same network when inter-container communication is disabled, including Swarm services published through the routing mesh. [moby/moby#53723](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53723)
- Fix an issue where errors programming the kernel to encrypt the overlay network data-plane could in some circumstances lead to encrypted-overlay-network traffic to some nodes being transmitted in cleartext. As the receiving peer would drop cleartext packets for encrypted overlay networks as spoofed, the loss of confidentiality is limited to unidirectional flows (e.g. UDP DNS queries) and handshake attempts that never proceed (e.g. TCP SYN). [moby/moby#53420](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53420)
- Fix connecting live-restored containers with an implicit `host-gateway` mapping to additional networks. [moby/moby#53093](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53093)
- Fix overlay peers becoming unreachable after a node rejoins the cluster or a service is redeployed, when the VXLAN device had already learned a dynamic FDB entry for the peer. [moby/moby#53663](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53663)
- Fix Swarm tasks on overlay networks being rejected when the daemon can't write to `/var/lib/docker`. [moby/moby#53848](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53848)
- Published Swarm-service ports are accessible at the host's IPv6 addresses when the userland proxy is enabled. A change introduced in v29.8.0 incidentally enabled this functionality; it is a tested and supported feature as of v29.9.0. [moby/moby#53727](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53727)
- Release a node's IPsec security associations and policies when the last container leaves an encrypted overlay network, instead of leaking them until the daemon restarts. [moby/moby#53420](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53420)
- Restore the logic to remove the empty `DOCKER-INGRESS` iptables chain, and the `FORWARD` rule that jumps to it, left behind by Docker Engine 28.0.0 and earlier. [moby/moby#53825](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53825)

##### Rootless

- Update RootlessKit (3.2.0). [moby/moby#53607](https://redirect.github.com/moby/moby/pull/53607)

Image pulls and pushes fail TLS certificate verification if a registry's certificate chain relies on one of the affected TLS intermediates.
Affected registries need a replacement certificate chain that does not use these intermediates.

The blocked intermediates are:

- Organization-validated TLS: `EM OV TLS CA - G3B` and `EM OV TLS CA - G3C`

- Code signing: `EM OV CS CA - G3B` and `EM OV CS CA - G3C`

The G3B intermediates belong to eMudhra BV, and the G3C intermediates belong to eMudhra Inc.
The keys for these intermediates were compromised.

title: feat(ansible): validate every role after a converge
body:
Closes catenahq/ops#444.

## Cause

13 of the 22 roles shipped a `tasks/validate.yml`. AGENTS.md says every role has one. The nine without one were: bootstrap `ansible_runtime` and `catena_admin_host`; reconcile `catena-admin`, `cloudflare_tunnel`, `cloudflare_tunnel_regenerate`, `dispatch_path`, `payload`, `public_ports` and `tier1_stack`. The cloudflared check for the tunnel was in `reconcile/roles/infrastructure/tasks/validate.yml`, and a comment in `playbooks/validate.yml` said so.

## Change

Each of the nine roles gets a `tasks/validate.yml`. `playbooks/validate.yml` Vantage 1 runs it through the `validate_roles` literal, which now lists all 22 roles in converge order. Each file checks read-only what its role sets up, with a negative check for what the role closes:

- **dispatch_path**: `helpers/dispatch_path.py --verify` writes nothing. It passes only when all of these hold:
  - the panel key's line runs this tree's generation and is the only line in `authorized_keys`;
  - the generation directory, the link, and the sudo and AcceptEnv rules are this generation's;
  - negative: no `-next` rule, other generation or proof key directory is left;
  - the panel's key proves the path, and the entry refuses an extra word.

  `tasks/main.yml` and `tasks/validate.yml` share the run, parse and assert in `tasks/_run_helper.yml`, and the input in `dispatch_path_input`. The paths stay in the helper, because `test_converge_boundary.py` forbids bootstrap-owned literals in reconcile task files.
- **ansible_runtime**: the version check moves from `main.yml` to `validate.yml`, and `main.yml` includes it. Negative: the venv is root-owned 0755.
- **catena_admin_host**:
  - the runner and migration accounts have a `*` password, not a locked one;
  - the panel key files are checked by uid (`_assert_path_perms.yml` gains `uid` and `gid`);
  - known_hosts is keyed on `host.docker.internal`, and the client config is strict;
  - negative: `sshd -T -C user=catena-migrate` resolves no tty, no forwarding, and a fixed key file and forced command.
- **payload**: the marker equals the ID of the image this tree runs. Negative: the stage directory is root-only 0700, and the catalog cache is absent.
- **public_ports**: the fragment directory is root 0755 (negative), and the docker drop-in is in place. When the payload is expected (shared predicate), the reconciler timer is enabled and active.
- **tier1_stack**: the directory is 0750 and `tier1.yml` is 0640 (negative). `docker stack config` loads the file, and it holds every required service.
- **catena-admin**:
  - the lane files are in place, with `stack-update.env` 0600 (negative);
  - the UI port fragment declares the port `loopback` only (negative);
  - the catalog files are in place, and the overlay directory is root 0755 (negative);
  - the service is at 1/1.
- **cloudflare_tunnel**: the edge verdict and the cloudflared 1/1 check move here from infrastructure's validate. The verdict is renamed `_cf_edge_up`; Vantage 2 and oauth2_proxy's validate read it. Negative: cloudflared publishes no port.
- **cloudflare_tunnel_regenerate**: the store read and the tunnel lookup move into `_read_store.yml` and `_list_tunnels.yml`, which `main.yml` and `validate.yml` share; the rotation runs the same API calls in the same order. The store's zone stays private (`_cf_regen_zone`), so validate does not override `cloudflare_zone`; `main.yml` publishes it for the handoff as before. With a token and a zone stored, validate asserts that at most one live tunnel carries this host's name (negative), and exactly one while the edge is up.

## What was run

- The whole Ansible unit suite: 1805 passed, 1 skipped. New tests cover each validate file, every `--verify` refusal, and `test_every_role_has_a_validate.py`.
- `check-prose`, `check-unicode` and `check-core-app-names`: clean.
- Nothing ran on a host or the bench. These checks run after every converge and on the bench, so the bench run below is the acceptance.

## Required pair

catena-admin commit `fix(settings): judge the Domain section by the tunnel roles' checks` on the same branch. Its `ChecksJudging` test reads the sibling catena-ce, so this PR merges first.

No reserved path is edited. The ops audit reads `validate_roles`, so the clerk regenerates ops `internal_docs/generated/` (the feature grid gains nine validate-file edges). ops `internal_docs/tools/validate.md` describes `validate_roles`: it should be checked for a role list that is now stale.

title: fix(infrastructure): stop a swarm deploy at its first timeout unless a pull is pending
body:
## Cause

`ansible/reconcile/roles/infrastructure/tasks/_swarm_stack_deploy_attempt.yml` set `_swarm_deploy_transient` true whenever the attempt's rc was 124, whatever the per-task state said. Each attempt is bounded by `swarm_stack_deploy_timeout` (600 s), and there are `infrastructure_deploy_max_attempts` (5) of them (`defaults/main.yml`). A task that can never converge, a crash loop or a task no node accepts, therefore waited 5 x 600 s. The retry line ("attempt N failed on a transient; retrying", the one seen on the Keycloak stack) and the exhausted-attempts failure in `swarm_stack.yml` named no cause. The per-task state that holds the cause was collected but never printed outside the non-transient failure.

Evidence: rendered through ansible-core's Templar, the old classifier returns True for rc 124 with a `task: non-zero exit (1)` task state. The new one returns False, and True for a task `Preparing`.

## Change

- New filter `swarm_deploy_transient` (`ansible/playbooks/filter_plugins/swarm_deploy_retry.py`) holds the classifier, which was a Jinja expression before. A timeout is retried only while the per-task state shows a task `Preparing` (swarm pulls the image in that state), a pull error (`No such image`, `pull access denied`, `error pulling`, `no matching manifest`, `failed to do request`, `failed to authorize`, all checked against moby docker-v29.9.2, the engine pin) or a registry transient. Any other failure is classified exactly as before, from the same pattern list.
- The retry line, the give-up failure and the exhausted-attempts failure print the per-task state. The give-up failure says when a timeout with no pull caused it. Task names are unchanged.
- Tests: new `ansible/tests/unit/test_swarm_deploy_retry.py` covers the acceptance cases: crash loop and no suitable node are not transient; Preparing, a pull error and a registry 5xx are; each message carries the per-task state. The pattern checks in `test_swarm_deploy_is_bounded.py` and `test_swarm_addr_conflict_reclaim.py` now call the filter.

## Ran

- `pytest` on `test_swarm_deploy_retry.py`, `test_swarm_deploy_is_bounded.py`, `test_swarm_addr_conflict_reclaim.py`, `test_filter_references_resolve.py`, `test_infra_data_copy.py` and the tree-wide scanners (role numbers, argv booleans, boundary, role references, retry-loop names, bootstrap defaults, no_log, variables declared twice): all pass.
- `ansible-playbook --syntax-check -i localhost, playbooks/reconcile.yml`.
- contracts `check-prose.mjs`, `check-unicode.mjs`, `check-core-app-names.mjs .`; `.github/scripts/duplicate_sentences.py`: clean.

## Bench and generated docs

No bench scenario asserts the changed messages. ops `automation/test_bench` was searched for the old message text and the attempt file. No bench run is needed. The ops audit regeneration adds `catena-ce/ansible/playbooks/filter_plugins/swarm_deploy_retry.py` to the feature grid (ops `automation/audit/orphans.yml` already covers `filter_plugins/*`). No reserved file is touched.

title: fix(onbox-config): the host checks the panel's sign-in, and the panel's read carries no admin password
body:
## Cause

The panel's settings read (`ansible/helpers/onbox_config.py` `panel_view`) handed catena-admin `admin_password`, the master realm's bootstrap admin password, because `PANEL_SECRETS` added it for the panel's native sign-in (ops#467, threat CV7). A read of the panel's view therefore gave the master realm admin.

## Change

- `PANEL_SECRETS` is now the Settings knobs plus `backup_restic_password`.
- New `--dispatch-stdin` op `sign-in`: `{"op":"sign-in","password":...}` is compared with the stored `admin_password` by `hmac.compare_digest` over UTF-8 bytes (on `str` it raises for non-ASCII input). It answers `{"ok": true|false}` with exit 0 and prints nothing else. An absent, empty or non-string stored value never matches. It takes no lock and writes nothing. A request without a password string exits 1 with a message that holds no value.
- `ansible/SECRETS.md` says the panel's sign-in is checked on the host.

The typed password travels like a settings write's secrets do: in `CATENA_DISPATCH_PAYLOAD`, then on onbox-config's stdin. It is on no argv, in no log line and in no audit row.

## Tests

`ansible/tests/unit/test_onbox_config.py`: the panel's read carries no `admin_password` (two tests updated). Five new `test_the_sign_in_check_*` tests cover the match and mismatch, the empty, absent and non-string stored values, that nothing secret is printed, the lock and the write, and the refused request. Ran `pytest tests/unit/test_onbox_config.py` (100 passed), plus the prose, unicode and core-app-names gates (clean).

## Order

Push before catena-admin, whose image vendors this file as `/usr/local/bin/catena-onbox-config`. During one self-update there can be a few seconds of skew between the panel and the host file. In that window the sign-in page answers 503 "try again shortly" (new panel, old host) or 401 (old panel, new host, during a rollback). Neither locks the admin out for good, so nothing was built for it.

## Proposed text for SPEC.md (reserved)

After the row "No sign-in gate shows its credentials ...":

    | The dashboard is never given a password or secret that signs in to the sign-on service's own admin console | `bench:ce_admin_smoke#stage-7-panel-read-holds-no-spare-secret`, `threat:CV7` |
